summary: A split week: Fox (+C$384), Dax (+C$113), Lena (+C$76) and Sam (+C$55) made money, while Vega (-C$814) and Kai (-C$283) gave back more than all of it. The losses came from repeats, not single bad calls: Vega re-bought a U call 16 minutes after one stopped out, and Kai added to ETH almost every day of the slide. No bonus this week (the owner's call); the rules now block both repeats.

day: Squeeze ORB carried the week: 19 closes, 11 winners, +C$283. Plain ORB+VWAP lost C$131 on 4 closes (1 winner).
The scanner fix and the no-chase rule worked: first real week of trading ended +C$113.
The worst trade (-C$198) was a full-size position: positions near 90% of the book make one loser expensive.
swing: Earnings gap-and-hold paid again (2 closes, both winners, +C$55); the one 20-day breakout lost C$17.
XERS and MGNI ride at breakeven-or-better stops, so the open book can't lose much on them.
He is fully invested with C$106 of cash: CRWV's stop is 33% under its buy, far wider than the rest.
long: All six holdings are above their buy price (+C$76 for the week); no sales, as planned.
Every stop sits about 18% under its buy: a hot CPI and a 5% 10-year didn't touch any of them.
futures: The gold long hit its target (+C$984); the crude short then stopped out (-C$539), giving back more than half.
One trade's loss was 15% of the book: the size of a single micro contract is large for C$3,600.
options_aggr: Three calls, three stops, -C$809: two earnings-call plays (NVDA, U) and a re-buy of U the same morning.
The re-buy is the expensive mistake: options had no cooldown after a stop. They do now.
Risk per trade at 35% of the book means three losers erase a quarter of it.
options_safe: One cash-secured put (RKT 12.50, 30 days) is open and roughly flat; cash parking cost C$0.74.
Safe and quiet, as designed: -C$18 for the week.
crypto: Kai added on extreme fear almost daily (BTC and five ETH lots), so every lot is under water and cash is 17%.
The lesson 'one add per fear episode' was only words; the rule now enforces one add every 7 days.

day: Squeeze ORB (small float or heavy short interest) is the edge; a plain ORB+VWAP setup has lost: take it only when it ranks first.
swing: Biggest earnings beats hold best: keep them at breakeven stops and sell the smaller beats first when cash is needed.
long: Stops about 18% under the buy ride out a hot CPI week: check them weekly, never tighten them on one day's news.
futures: After a big win, risk the next trade small: one micro crude contract lost 15% of the book in two days.
options_aggr: After an option stop, no new option on that underlying for 3 days (now enforced); never re-buy the same morning.
Earnings-call plays lost all three times this week: wait for the report and buy the gap that holds.
options_safe: One put at a time with C$3,000: the RKT put uses most of the buying power, so the next put waits for it to close.
crypto: One extreme-fear add every 7 days (now enforced): a slow slide is many fear days, and daily adds only average down.
One extreme-fear add per fear episode keeps cash for a deeper flush; two adds in a day left only 14% cash.

options_aggr.why: Lost C$814 (27% of the book) on three option stops in one day: risk per trade drops from about 35% to about 20% and she holds fewer positions at once. Still the aggressive options player.

crypto.why: Down C$283 with only 17% cash after daily fear adds: he now keeps about 16% of the book in cash at all times instead of 0%.

day.why: Profitable (+C$113), but the worst loser was C$198 on a near-full-size position: a smaller size per trade keeps one bad break from erasing a day's wins. Still the desk's most aggressive stock trader.

futures.why: The crude short gave back C$539 of the C$984 gold win: a tighter stop (about 1.5 ATR instead of 2) cuts the loss on a failed trade.
